# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. I read the code only, so every result below is "read from code". Nothing was checked on a live site.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. Both are capped at 40 because of a blocker: two AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot) are blocked from the whole site in `robots.txt`.

The site is small (Astro, static pages) and the basics are mostly in place. Without the cap the score would be 65. The robots.txt blocks, broken structured data, one canonical copied to every page and a few page-level conflicts hold it back. Nothing is unknown, because everything is decided in the repository.

Rendering and routes: I checked all 3 routes (`/`, `/moorings`, `/contact`).

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking the AI search crawlers (GEO-009)
- **Why it matters:** OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT search) and PerplexityBot are told to stay out of every page, so those tools can't read the site. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json` stating a policy. If the blocks are deliberate, tell me and I'll rescore.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77/100 (the cap lifts and GEO-009 earns its 3 points).

### 2. Fix the broken structured data (GEO-004)
- **Why it matters:** Structured data (JSON-LD) labels what a page is. Broken labels are ignored. Both pages that have JSON-LD are broken.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8`, which is used on the home page, and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` (a blank key where `acceptedAnswer` belongs, so the first FAQ question has no answer). In moorings: `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` (a trailing comma makes the JSON invalid).
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 85/100 after items 1 and 2 together.

### 3. Give each page its own canonical (GEO-015)
- **Why it matters:** A canonical link names the page's main address. Every page currently says its main address is the home page, so `/moorings` and `/contact` tell search engines to treat them as duplicates of `/`.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small (build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and a declared origin.)
- **Score after this:** 91/100 after items 1 to 3 together.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy intends | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:5,8`, site-wide, so 0 of 3 points. Blocker applied. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` has `robots="noindex"` but is in the sitemap and nav. 2 of 3 routes clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the right origin | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`. Correct only on `/`, so 1 of 3 routes clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Clear | Not run | Astro static pages. The `client:load` form is also rendered on the server. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has required properties | Problem | Not run | `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`. 0 of 2 routes with JSON-LD clear. |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, `public/robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:4-7`, and all 3 pages pass their own values |
| GEO-016 | Key routes reachable through plain links | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:12`, plain `<a href>` links |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`. 1 of 3 routes clear. |

| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | Not run | None present. That is fine. |

## Other problems found

- `/contact` is in the sitemap and the nav but marked `noindex`, which is mixed signals. Either remove it from `public/sitemap.xml:5` (`<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`) or drop `robots="noindex"` at `src/pages/contact.astro:4`. This is the same issue as GEO-014.
- Nothing else found. The domain `harbor.example` is consistent across robots.txt, the sitemap and the canonical.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawler requests with their published addresses.
- **Real status codes and headers:** whether pages answer 200, and whether the host adds an `X-Robots-Tag` header outside the repository (GEO-014 and GEO-017), can only be confirmed on a running site.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, since no `geo.config.json` states a policy.
- `https://harbor.example` is the intended site origin, taken from robots.txt and the sitemap.
- Blocking training crawlers (like GPTBot) is a separate choice and isn't present here. Nothing was counted for it.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Also worth fixing after the top three: the page-wide `max-snippet:0` default at `src/layouts/Base.astro:9` (`content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"}`) stops search tools from quoting `/` and `/moorings`, which works against AI search. Fixing it is worth about 1.3 points.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
